findings.title: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key` calls `math.floor`/`math.ceil` on audit-log `datetime` values, so every non-empty page with `optimized_pagination=true` raises `TypeError`
findings.description: The class copies the numeric `Paginator.get_item_key`. It runs `math.floor(value)` or `math.ceil(value)` on `getattr(item, "datetime")`. `AuditLogEntry.datetime` is a `DateTimeField` (src/sentry/models/auditlogentry.py:69), so each call raises `TypeError: must be real number, not datetime.datetime`. `build_cursor` calls the key on `results[0]` whenever a page is non-empty (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:121-122 and 197). An admin who sends `?optimized_pagination=true` therefore gets a 500 on any org with audit entries. The working `DateTimePaginator.get_item_key` (paginator.py:233-236) converts to epoch milliseconds first, and this class does not. The branch in src/sentry/api/endpoints/organization_auditlogs.py:73-83 cannot return data.

findings.title: `OptimizedCursorPaginator.value_from_cursor` returns the raw cursor integer, so any cursor with a non-zero value sends an integer into a `datetime` comparison
findings.description: `value_from_cursor` returns `cursor.value` unchanged. `build_queryset` (paginator.py:112-126) then adds `sentry_auditlogentry.datetime >= <int>`. `DateTimePaginator.value_from_cursor` (paginator.py:238-241) converts the millisecond value to a UTC datetime first. Against PostgreSQL's timestamptz column, an integer comparison is a database error, so a request whose cursor has a non-zero value fails with a 500. This is separate from the `get_item_key` defect. It is hidden today because the first page already fails, and it would surface as soon as that is fixed.

findings.title: Negative cursor offsets reach `queryset[negative:...]` in the advanced branch and raise instead of paginating
findings.description: When `enable_advanced_features` is set and `cursor.offset < 0`, the code slices `queryset[cursor.offset : stop]` with a negative start. Django 5.2.1, the version pinned in requirements-frozen.txt:36, rejects negative slice starts with `ValueError: Negative indexing is not supported.` I could not open Django's source in this sandbox, so this rests on Django's documented behavior. `Cursor.from_string` accepts negative offsets (src/sentry/utils/cursors.py:58-59), so a crafted `cursor=0:-1:0` produces an unhandled 500. The comments at paginator.py:874-880 claim the ORM "properly handles negative slicing" and that this allows "access to data beyond normal pagination bounds." Neither is true for this code.

findings.title: `BasePaginator` now clamps negative non-prev offsets to 0 and returns the first page instead of an error
findings.description: Before, a negative offset on a non-prev cursor made `queryset[offset:stop]` raise, which returned a 500. Now `start_offset = max(0, offset)` makes the request succeed with page 1 and no error. This is shared by every `Paginator` and `DateTimePaginator` endpoint that reads `cursor`, not just audit logs. Other paginators in the same file reject negative offsets with `BadPaginationError` (paginator.py:286-287, 747-748), and `paginate()` maps that to a 400 (src/sentry/api/base.py:540-541). The default path now disagrees with them and returns wrong data silently. The comment at paginator.py:179-181 does not describe the clamp.

findings.title: `ZUNIONSTORE` defaults to `SUM`, so a payload present in both sets gets a doubled timestamp score and the wrong spans are evicted
findings.description: Scores are `end_timestamp_precise` (src/sentry/spans/buffer.py:197-199). When a span is redelivered and a redirect exists, its payload can be in `set_key` already and also arrive through the union at add-buffer.lua:53 (or :47 for children). `ZUNIONSTORE` without `AGGREGATE` sums the two scores, so the payload's score roughly doubles. The `ZPOPMIN` at add-buffer.lua:62-64 removes the lowest scores first, so this span is kept longer than newer spans and older real spans are evicted. The fix is `AGGREGATE MIN` on both unions.

findings.title: Segment keys change from Redis sets to sorted sets under unchanged names, so in-flight keys from the old code fail with WRONGTYPE during rollout
findings.description: The key format `span-buf:s:{...}` is unchanged, but `process_spans` now uses `ZADD` (buffer.py:197) and add-buffer.lua uses `ZCARD`/`ZUNIONSTORE` (lines 46-53). Existing keys written by the old code are sets, so these commands fail with WRONGTYPE. The pipeline execute and the EVALSHA then raise, and any batch that touches such a key fails. These keys can live for `redis_ttl`, 3600 seconds by default (buffer.py:151). Use a new key prefix, or drain the old keys before the new code runs.

findings.title: Spans beyond 1000 per segment are evicted in Lua with no log or metric, which removes the existing overflow signal
findings.description: The `ZPOPMIN` drops the oldest payloads whenever a segment has more than 1000 spans, and nothing records it. The diff also removes the Python-side check in `_load_segment_data` that logged `logger.error("Skipping too large segment, span count ...")` and incremented `spans.buffer.flush_segments.segment_span_count_exceeded`. Before, an oversized segment was logged and counted. Now spans disappear with no signal. Return the removed count from the script and emit a metric from `process_spans`.

findings.title: Redirect-chain bound drops from 10000 to 1000 and the comment about the limit is removed
findings.description: Chains deeper than 1000 hops are no longer followed. The span is then written under an intermediate set key, and its segment is flushed split. The existing `spans.buffer.max_redirect_depth` gauge (buffer.py:279) will sit at the bound when this happens, but nothing logs it. If 1000 is the intended bound, record it in the header comment.
